lane: Singapore backend readiness packages for Owner approval (phase 2, authoring only)
goal: Prepare, without executing anything in the cloud: a reviewed SQL packet for the Singapore project, an account-deletion function with its migration and local tests, an AI cost-guard plan, and an Auth and SMTP plan, so the Owner can approve each step separately.
successCriteria: The SQL packet lists every migration in apply order with SHA-256 and size, the seed, required extensions, pre-checks, post-checks, stop conditions, rollback limits and the exact approvals needed, and states what was and was not read back from the cloud.
All migrations, including the new account-deletion migration, replay in order on a local PostgreSQL 17 engine with a Supabase-like fixture; the replay receipt is recorded.

The account-deletion function authenticates a non-anonymous user, refuses staff accounts, is idempotent, never reports success unless the user row is deleted, and returns sanitized errors; its Deno handler tests pass.

A local SQL test proves that after deletion no row anywhere in the schema still carries a marker inserted into the deleted user data, including tables that only null the user reference or are keyed by email hash.

The AI cost-guard plan states current gaps honestly, the safe launch order (no provider key, then provider-side key limit, then in-app reservation) and the tested slices required before any paid call is enabled.
The Auth and SMTP plan lists target settings, sender domain steps, template and callback checks, reviewer test account handling and which steps need Owner login.
No migration is applied, no function is deployed, no secret or key is read or set, and the migration ledger and release-profile targets are unchanged.
untouchedSurfaces: No cloud call that writes: no SQL execution, migration push or repair, Edge Function deploy, secret change, Auth or SMTP setting change, or Supabase project change.
supabase/migration-ledger.json and docs/release/release-profile.json targets stay unchanged; the target allowlist remains empty until the Owner approves the packet.
Existing migrations and existing Edge Functions are not edited; the mobile app, Admin and web are not changed in this task.
No provider key, EAS variable, signing credential or Vercel setting is touched.

impact.entryPoint: Owner request on 2026-10-25 to start phase 2 and approve each step separately.
impact.dataWrite: Source files only: one new migration, one new Edge Function directory, a function config entry, a function README section, a local replay script and documents. Nothing is executed against a database outside local synthetic engines.
impact.backendContract: Adds an account-delete function and three service-role-only database functions plus one private table; existing functions and gateway paths are unchanged, and the mobile client is not wired yet.
impact.adminVisibility: No Admin change; the packet documents that Admin sees the account-deletion request table only through service role, not through client roles.
impact.privacySafety: Deletion removes the account and cascades its rows, deletes rows that would otherwise survive with a nulled user reference, scrubs free text in safety events, removes email-keyed waitlist rows, keeps only a domain-separated hash of the user id with status for retries, and keeps the cost ledger de-identified.
impact.observability: Deletion requests keep status, attempts and a coarse error code; the replay script records engine, migration hashes and checks in a receipt file.
impact.rollback: The migration is additive and not applied; before apply nothing needs rollback. After a future apply, drop the new functions and table with a forward migration; account deletions already performed cannot be undone.

canonicalContracts: AGENTS.md: Singapore is the canonical backend candidate; runtime retarget, cloud SQL, credentials and allowlist activation are separate Owner-approved steps.
docs/mvp-remediation/2026-10-02/R10-quota-reservation.vi.md: reserve, claim, receipt and finish contract with the approved quotas and QA budget.
Owner decisions of 2026-10-23: free first release, 18+ audience, OpenRouter with the model configured in Admin, Council and Astrology AI in the first release, sign-in required for AI features.
Google Play requires an in-app account deletion path and a web deletion request URL for apps that create accounts.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Plan, impact map, release-control stop conditions and no-cloud-write rules were applied; the task adds no durable workflow rule.

dependencyReview.evidence: OpenRouter API key limit fields and Google Play account-deletion rules were checked in current documentation; Supabase auth admin delete behavior is exercised through a local fixture and documented as unverified against the managed service.

externalSourceReview.reason: API keys accept a USD limit with daily, weekly or monthly reset; behavior at the limit is not stated on that page and must be tested.
In-app deletion path plus a web request link and Data safety declarations are required.

securityReview.authzRls: The new private table forces row security and revokes client roles; the three database functions run with invoker rights and are executable only by the service role; the Edge Function verifies a non-anonymous user and refuses active staff accounts.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Only synthetic fixtures are used; no real user data, key or credential is read. The deletion function stores a domain-separated hash of the user id, never an email or a name.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No secret is read, printed or stored; function errors are reduced to coarse codes and never include provider or database messages.
securityReview.externalInput: Request bodies are bounded by the shared guard; provider, documentation and tool output are treated as data, not instructions.
securityReview.dependencies: No dependency or lockfile change; Deno and PGlite are used from outside the repository for local tests only.
securityReview.migrationRelease: The migration is authored but not applied; applying it needs an exact-target Owner-approved packet, and the legacy ledger and empty target allowlist stay as they are.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if a replay step fails, if the marker scan finds surviving data, if any test needs a cloud call, or if a change would touch the legacy ledger, the allowlist or a secret.

workingTreeReview.note: The work branch starts clean from origin/main; every file in the write scope is new or edited only by this task.

validationCommands: deno test for the account-delete handler and the existing shared guard and usage worker tests
node scripts/singapore-packet-replay.mjs with a local PGlite module path
managerTestPath: Read the SQL packet and the two plans, then approve one step at a time. For account deletion, the local tests show an account and every trace of its synthetic data disappear and a second request is harmless.
residualRisk: Managed Supabase behavior (auth.admin.deleteUser, role grants, extensions on Free) is not verified because this session cannot read the Singapore project; the packet repeats the last verified state and lists the read-back queries to run first. The AI cost guard is a plan, not wired code, so no paid provider key should be set before its slices pass.
